hb_toll.text: The tolls are what they are. Take it up with the Humber Bridge Board, or the Queen. She opened it.
It moves a little in a gale. It is meant to. Don't look down, and don't look at the cyclists either, they look at nobody.

hb_historian.text: This is Ermine Street. Legions marched up it to York, in a straight line, with their own pots and pans on a pole.
A legionary carried about forty kilos. And you complain about a rucksack.

hb_farmer.text: Wolds soil is chalk and flint. Not a lot grows in it, except barley, and Lord, does barley grow. Half of what you drink started in a field like this.
That chap Tennyson grew up near here, at Somersby. Even the poets couldn't stay away from the Wolds.

hb_birdman.text: Reed beds don't look after themselves. I cut them each winter so the bitterns have something to hide in. Roof thatchers love the leftovers.
